one_sentence: Dark energy is structurally isomorphic to divine sustaining grace, with a dynamic Grace Function that evolves from creation to eternity and couples to collective consciousness.
executive_summary: This document establishes a structural isomorphism between dark energy in cosmology and divine sustaining grace in Christian theology. It proposes a Modified Friedmann Equation where the static cosmological constant Lambda is replaced by a dynamic Grace Function G(t, Psi_collective) that evolves from a maximum at creation to an eternal sustaining value, and couples to collective consciousness. The key evidence is the mathematical formulation of the Grace Function, which aims to resolve the cosmological constant problem (120 orders of magnitude discrepancy) and the Hubble tension (5 sigma discrepancy between local and CMB measurements). The conclusion is that dark energy, as the dominant component of the universe (~68% of energy density), maps functionally to the theological claim that God continuously sustains creation. The strongest part is the structural parallel; the weakest is the speculative consciousness coupling, which is currently unfalsifiable.
short_summary: This document is a structural isomorphism record (ISO-018) that maps dark energy to divine sustaining grace. The core structural claim is that the cosmological constant can be replaced by a dynamic Grace Function G(t, Psi_collective) that evolves from creation to eternity and couples to collective consciousness. The key evidence is the Modified Friedmann Equation E14.1 and the Grace Function D14.1, which together aim to resolve the cosmological constant problem and the Hubble tension. This matters because it provides a testable physical framework for the theological concept of continuous creation, with predictions (w != -1) that can be falsified by upcoming dark energy surveys.
